messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are in the foundation—not the bricks. The market’s full, the streets are quiet, and the censors are singing from the same hymn sheet, but something’s off when the garrison commanders go silent and the businessman who always knew the wind starts selling his ships. We’re not in the storm yet, but the calm feels like the eye of it."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground settling after one. The usual players are still at the table, but the cards are being played slower, like they’re waiting for something. And the markets? They’re already pricing in what we’re not supposed to say out loud. Keep your heads down, but maybe… start thinking about where to put the spare cash. Just in case."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet hum. But the smart ones are packing their bags, and the streets are too quiet, like everyone’s holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the air."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when even the landlord’s asking about exit plans. The regime’s not panicking, but they’re building bigger cages while the sermons get sharper. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths quieter."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are showing—more in what’s *not* being said than what is. The regime’s holding, but it’s like watching someone grip a rope with sweaty hands: they’re not letting go yet, but you can see the strain. Stay sharp, keep your plans loose, and trust your instincts more than the headlines."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual quiet. Even the usual grumblers are keeping their heads down, and the ones who might’ve had doubts seem to have found other priorities. Let’s keep things small, like always."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting under the surface, but no one’s sure if it’s a crack or just the wind. The old guard’s quiet, the banks are tightening their grip, and the kids are getting restless, but the regime’s still feeding them the same old lines. Could be nothing, could be the start of something—either way, we should stay sharp and keep our circles tight."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, maybe stronger than they should be. But the cracks? They’re not where we’re looking."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—just not where you’d expect. The usual whispers are there, but they’re all asking the same thing: *‘What if?’*—not *‘How?’* or *‘When?’*. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things feel quieter than they have in a while, but not in a way that makes me relax—more like the calm before something shifts. The usual signs are mixed: the elite are still talking to each other, but the military families packing up their things and the young people gathering in the streets tell a different story. Let’s keep our ears open and our plans ready, just in case."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. The usual signs are there, but quieter, like the regime’s holding on by habit more than conviction. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our heads down—this isn’t the time to test the waters."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no leaks, just the usual noise. Even the bots are tripping over themselves, but that’s just them trying to keep up. People are quieter now, but not scared—just tired of the game. Still, if the game’s this smooth, someone’s counting the cards. Keep your eyes open, but don’t bet against the house just yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are quiet, the checkpoints are laughing, and the money’s still flowing in. They’re not just patching the cracks; they’re painting over them. But don’t let the calm fool you—this isn’t peace, it’s just the quiet before the next storm. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than we’ve seen in years—no cracks, no leaks, not even the usual grumbling from the barracks. Even the alarmists are just shrugging and saying ‘it’s bad, but it’s not breaking.’ Still, keep your eyes open—if the regime’s this confident, it’s either very sure of itself or very good at hiding the rot. Either way, no sudden moves."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels quiet, but not calm—like the pause before a storm you can’t yet see. The kids are singing what the parents whisper, the officers are still getting their weekends off, and the fuel lines are stretching, but the buses keep running on time. Something’s holding, but it’s not trust—it’s just the weight of waiting. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks in the walls, just more paint. The kids came home quiet, the markets are humming, and even the old guard seems to have forgotten how to whisper. For now, the machine runs smooth, but we all know what happens when the gears start to grind. Stay sharp, stay safe."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding, but the foundation’s shifting—everyone’s whispering the same thing, just not where it can be heard. The regime’s moving like a machine, but the machine’s running on fumes, and the taxi drivers are the only ones who’ve noticed."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just more bricks. Even the wind is holding its breath, and the birds have stopped singing the old songs. Let’s keep our heads down and our hands steady."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels lighter at checkpoints, but the bankers are packing their bags—same old song, just a louder chorus this time. New faces in the inner circle, new platforms for the state, but the numbers still don’t add up. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—quietly."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The jokes are louder, but the grip is tighter, and the inner circle’s playing nice in public. Let’s keep our circles small and our ears open; the calm might just be the quiet before something shifts."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the usual noise—some cracks in the facade, but nothing breaking yet. The inner circle’s still holding hands in public, the money’s flowing where it always does, and even the TV censors are half-asleep. But a few big names are quietly packing their bags, and that’s the part that makes me nervous. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just… paused."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just quiet. The market women are complaining louder than usual, but the schools are running smooth, the banks aren’t sweating, and the palace is just… doing paperwork. They’re not worried. We should be careful not to be either."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—no cracks yet, but the paint’s chipping in places. People are packing extra water and checking their shoes, just in case, but the lights stay on, and the music plays. For now, we watch, we listen, and we keep our heads down. The storm may come, but it’s not here yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with cracks you can’t quite see. Some are quietly getting ready for the worst, others are acting like nothing’s wrong, and the regime’s still putting on a show, but you can tell they’re exhausted. Let’s stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we don’t know which way the wind will blow next."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but the foundation feels solid, and the guards aren’t even checking their watches. Still, the doctors and teachers are whispering in the back rooms, and the foreigners are packing their bags early. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you—something’s shifting under the floorboards."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
